//: The ONE source of truth for how every recipe is typechecked. scripts/build-recipes.mjs reads
this file through the TypeScript compiler API rather than re-stating flags, so the strictness
an editor shows you and the strictness CI enforces cannot drift apart.
`verbatimModuleSyntax` is REQUIRED, not a preference: the .mjs a reader runs is produced by
ts-blank-space, which erases type syntax without consulting the type checker. It therefore
cannot know that `import { Foo }` was only ever used as a type — so a type-only import MUST be
written `import type { Foo }` or it survives into the JS as a real import of a symbol that does
not exist at runtime. This flag makes that a compile error instead of a broken recipe.
No `paths`, no `baseUrl`: each recipe resolves `@cendor/*` and every provider SDK from its OWN
node_modules, which is what proves a copy-pasteable package.json actually works.
`@types/node` is the one exception, and it lives in scripts/ deliberately. It is a TYPECHECK
dependency, not a runtime one — `node index.mjs` has never needed it — so putting it in all 52
recipe manifests would misrepresent the pins a reader copies and hand dependabot 52 directories
of noise for a types package. typeRoots is relative to THIS file, so one copy serves every recipe.
